{{Short description|French physicist (born 1969)}}
{{Expand French|topic=bio|Philippe Bouyer|date=June 2020}}

{{Infobox scientist|image=File:Philippe Bouyer.jpg|field=physics|education={{hlist|Institut d'Optique|Laboratoire Kastler Brossel}}}}

Philippe Bouyer (born 7 March 1969) is a French physicist and researcher, professor at the University of Amsterdam and the Technical University of Eindhoven, and chairman of the Dutch Quantum Initiative, Quantum Delta NL. He co-founded Muquans, acquired later by Exail, a company specializing in quantum technology-based gravimeters.<ref name="nsr">{{cite journal|title=Gravity measurements below 10−9 g with a transportable absolute quantum gravimeter|journal=Scientific Reports|volume=8|issue=1|pages=12300|publisher=[[Scientific Reports]]|doi=10.1038/s41598-018-30608-1|doi-access=free|pmid=30120334|pmc=6098009|year=2018|last1=Ménoret|first1=Vincent|last2=Vermeulen|first2=Pierre|last3=Le Moigne|first3=Nicolas|last4=Bonvalot|first4=Sylvain|last5=Bouyer|first5=Philippe|last6=Landragin|first6=Arnaud|last7=Desruelle|first7=Bruno|bibcode=2018NatSR...812300M|arxiv=1809.04908}}</ref>

From 2011 to 2022, Bouyer was the founding director of the Laboratory for Photonics, Numerics, and Nano-sciences (LP2N) in Talence, France. He also was deputy director of the [[Institut d'Optique Graduate School]] from 2017 to 2022. Since 2019, he has been the Editor-in-Chief of ''AVS Quantum Science'', a journal published by AIP Publishing in partnership with the American Vacuum Society.<ref name="aip">{{cite web|url=https://publishing.aip.org/about/news/avs-quantum-science-takes-flight-with-philippe-bouyer/|title=AVS Quantum Science Takes Flight with Philippe Bouyer|publisher=AIP Publishing|year=2019}}</ref>

Bouyer is a graduate of the Institut d'Optique Graduate School, and he obtained his PhD in 1994 from the Laboratoire Kastler Brossel at the École Normale Supérieure. After joining the [[French National Center for Scientific Research]] (CNRS), his research concentrated on ultracold atoms, atom lasers, and Anderson localization.<ref name="AL">{{cite web|url=http://www.2physics.com/2008/07/anderson-localization-of-matter-waves.html|title=Anderson Localization of Matter-Waves|publisher=2physics.com|year=2008}}</ref> His current research interests include matter-wave interferometry for testing general relativity in microgravity conditions<ref name="ICE">{{cite web|url=https://sciences-techniques.cnes.fr/en/web/CNES-en/10166-st-2011-developing-more-accurate-accelerometers.php|title=Developing more accurate accelerometers|date=23 April 2015 |publisher = CNES}}</ref> and the detection of gravitational waves.<ref name="MIGA">{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fjse3xbCMnU|title=MIGA: Gravitational antenna based on atomic interferometry|website=[[YouTube]]|year=2021}}</ref>

In 2012, Bouyer received the Louis D. Award from the Institut de France for his scientific contributions.<ref name="louisD">{{cite web|url=http://grands-prix.institut-de-france.fr/philippe-bouyer|title=Le Prix scientifique 2012 de la Fondation Louis D. a été attribué conjointement à Philippe Bouyer et Christophe Salomon.|date=2012}}</ref> He is also a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] (APS) and a senior member of the [[Optical Society of America]] (OSA).
